correctness.rationale: Let the three positive clockwise spacings sum to n. At n≥3k−1 at least one is long (≥k). Pair correlations at offsets below k are recovered by summing the observed counts of factors containing the two specified ones. If no factor sees all three ones, no two consecutive spacings sum to less than k, and those correlations exactly give the multiset of short spacings. The empty and singleton correlations are fixed; with the triple correlations zero, Boolean inclusion–exclusion recovers the full spectrum from the pair correlations. If a factor sees all three markers, it specifies the ordered short spacings and the total n fixes the remaining long one, so the source is fixed up to rotation. There are respectively 1_{n≥3k}, k−1, binom(k,2)−floor((k−1)^2/4), and binom(k−1,2) labels. Every label is realized in its stated range. Marking the unique short spacing in B or unique long spacing in C and D gives n placements per ordered cyclic configuration. For A, an indexed word with a distinguished marker has n times the number of weak compositions of n−3k into three parts as its total count over all words; division by three handles periodic words without a freeness assumption. These yield every stated fiber size, also for k=2, and the deficit of exactly one label at n=3k−1 proves permanent stabilization at 3k.
residual_risks: An independent direct window enumeration reported agreement on 27 cases and 37,764 indexed words, not a proof of the general law; the proof is combinatorial.

broader_coverage.reasoning: In the frozen range at most two gaps are short. The prior invariant then leaves just zero, one, or two short spacings with sum at least k, and the known unique-necklace case leaves the ordered short pairs with sum less than k. This is a restriction of the prior structural description.

Indexed fiber counts are direct weak-composition counts or n placements per ordered pattern, with the distinguished-marker correction in A. The nearby e75b073e3080 record instead observes compositions of linear windows.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Zero gaps g and positive spacings d satisfy d=g+1, so g<k−1 iff d<k. Passing from necklaces to indexed inputs does not change equality of observed spectra; only orbit sizes change. The known classes become A–C without a three-one factor and D with one.

originality.rationale: The earlier 2026-10-26 three-marker reconstruction record contains a stronger gap-spectrum lemma in its proof. On the same observation model it already classifies equality of all spectra lacking a three-one factor, and proves uniqueness up to rotation whenever such a factor is present. Its theorem about reconstruction length is not the decisive overlap; the underlying lemma and triple-factor argument cover the entire equivalence classification asserted here. The new displayed numbers follow mechanically by counting those known labels and their indexed realizations.

value.rationale: Exact channel sizes and collision fibers are useful quantities, but this frozen claim is a routine enumeration of the already characterized classes after imposing the at-most-two-short-spacings condition. It adds no independent structural step beyond a change of coordinates and elementary counts of labeled placements. The formulas are correct and convenient, but not a distinct scientific contribution under the stated standard.
residual_risks: The judgment does not deny the utility of consulting the closed forms.
